caveats: With one seed, target evidence uses the simulation's true noise SD (an oracle); a real one-seed experiment must borrow it, so one-seed power is optimistic. With two or more seeds the frozen rule estimates it from the seeds.

Power at a given slope is a location shift: the simulated DataDecide-structure truths have mean true slopes of about 2 to 4 points per decade, so power at +11.7 and +5.85 assumes the slope's sampling error does not depend on its size.
100 worlds per design: power near 0.8 carries a Monte Carlo SE of about 0.04.
Training compute counts every rung, including the target rung, which dominates it.
